analyst_view.overall: Early view: leaders PSV host Telstar, who are 16th on 10 points. PSV play Atlético Madrid at home in the Champions League on Wednesday 9 December, so this Sunday lunchtime game comes four days later and some rotation is possible. One match report says PSV recently beat Willem II 7-0 at home, a sign of how one-sided these games can get.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.3 goals. PSV's big home wins point higher, but the Atlético game four days earlier may lead PSV to rest players and ease off once ahead. Those two pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the site's figure.

corners.text: The numbers say 11 corners. I lean a little higher because Telstar are likely to sit deep and PSV push the full-backs high, which tends to produce blocked crosses and corners even with a rotated side.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards. I lean lower: one-sided games against a team defending deep usually have few fouls from the favourite, and there is no rivalry here. The referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots. PSV should dominate the ball, but a rotated line-up after a Champions League night can slow the tempo, so I keep the site's number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 shots on target. I see no news that moves this either way this far out; it depends on how strong a side PSV pick after the Atlético game.
